claims.text: Moderate-temperature thermal aging promotes diffusion-driven phase separation in non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Thermal aging causes precipitation of Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
Thermal aging causes Mg-rich intermetallic phases to segregate at grain boundaries.
The phase evolution modifies the alloy's surface chemistry.
Compared with the as-cast state, the aged alloy develops a more protective and adherent oxide scale during high-temperature oxidation.
The aging-induced microstructural evolution alters aqueous corrosion behavior relative to the as-cast state.
The initial alloy is an as-cast, non-equilibrium alloy with density below 6 g/cm3.
The initial microstructure is a metastable, relatively homogeneous mixture of a solid-solution matrix and dispersed precursor phases.
A moderate-temperature isothermal anneal below the melting point can induce diffusion-controlled phase separation.
Mg atoms diffuse and segregate during aging to form discrete Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates at grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
The evolved Mg-rich features facilitate heterogeneous nucleation of a more continuous and adherent high-temperature oxide layer.
Redistributed Mg-rich phases change local electrochemical properties and therefore change corrosion pathways.
The more protective oxide scale increases high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast baseline.
Redistribution of Mg-rich phases may improve overall corrosion performance, although localized corrosion variations may occur.
The as-cast baseline has a relatively uniform microstructure with minimal Mg segregation.
The as-cast baseline has less-developed oxide-scale characteristics than the aged condition.
The proposed mechanism is limited to non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with density below 6 g/cm3.
Similar thermal histories have been reported to both enhance corrosion protection and promote localized galvanic effects.
There is a consensus that the evolved oxide scale improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
